text:
devin: Quick check — I'm proposing we deprecate the legacy per-route quota headers (X-Quota-Limit, X-Quota-Remaining, X-Quota-Reset) and standardize on `X-Quota-V2-*`. Want to confirm the compatibility story before I open the RFC.

anika: +1 on the consolidation, but need clear fallback semantics. clients should still be able to rely on the old headers for a transition window.

maria: Agreed. Minimal disruption goal: keep both header families for a period, add a machine-readable deprecation signal, and provide a migration guide.

dryan: tagging @ryan for SDK implications — do we want SDKs to prefer V2 but fall back automatically?

ryan: yes. SDK behavior proposal: parse V2 if present; if not, parse legacy. Log a one-time deprecation warning per process run. No breaking change in decoding.

devin: proposed responses examples (for 429):
```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Quota-V2-Limit: 120
X-Quota-V2-Remaining: 0
X-Quota-V2-Reset: 1700000000
Deprecation: \"true; date=2025-09-30\"
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"rate_limited","message":"Per-route quota exceeded"}
```

maria: add a header hint for SDKs to know the canonical header name, e.g. `X-Quota-Canonical: X-Quota-V2`. That way proxies can rewrite if necessary.

anika: +1. Also we should emit a `Retry-After` when possible. Some clients rely solely on that.

devin: good call. updated example with Retry-After and an alternate-case for legacy headers:
```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Quota-V2-Limit: 120
X-Quota-V2-Remaining: 0
X-Quota-V2-Reset: 1700000000
X-Quota-Canonical: X-Quota-V2
Retry-After: 30
Deprecation: \"true; date=2025-09-30\"
```

ryan: timeline proposal for SDK teams: emit warning in next minor SDK (no breaking changes), then default to parsing V2-first in the minor after that, and remove legacy parsing in 6 months after deprecation date.

maria: ops question — can runtime emit both sets consistently across dedicated/dedicated-private? we need to avoid mixing (V2 on some hosts, legacy on others) during rollout.

sre-bot: perf note: adding extra headers negligible, but ensure proxies (CDN) aren't configured to strip unknown headers. Recommend escaping in our CDN config.

anika: rollout plan draft:
- week 0: announce deprecation + migration guide, SDK heads-up, console banner
- week 1-4: runtime emits both header sets + X-Quota-Canonical + Deprecation banner
- week 5-12: SDKs default to prefer V2, continue fallback, increase telemetry counts
- month 4-6: Sunset legacy header parsing in SDKs and publish breaking-note (depending on telemetry)

devin: PR checklist for RFC: exact header names, canonical header, sample responses for 200/429, SDK guidance, CDN/ingress notes, console telemetry keys. I'll draft tonight.

ryan: small SDK nit: expose a helper that returns a normalized quota struct: {limit, remaining, reset, source} where source is `v2` or `legacy` so apps can choose to log/migrate behavior.

maria: migration doc needs a section on tests — how to simulate mixed header environments and examples for our smoke tests.

anika: +emoji:thumbsup: I'll coordinate with QA to add an integration test that hits the canary runtime with both header sets.

sre-bot: adding a post-deploy monitor alert to surface any 429 spikes beyond baseline during the first 2 weeks.

devin: awesome — if no objections I'll open RFC + draft changelog and tag SDK and infra. Thanks everyone.

ryan: thanks — can you ping `#eng-sre` when RFC is live so infra can pre-check CDN config?

devin: will do.

sdk-bot: RFC created: https://reviews.example/redwood/rfcs/234 (auto)

maria: I left inline comments on the RFC about canonical header examples and test vectors.

anika: leaving this thread open for a few hours for async q's, otherwise I'll mark accepted by EOD.

ryan: quick Q — do we need to version the header schema beyond V2 for different quota models (per-user vs per-route)?

devin: keep V2 generic for now; if we need extension we can add a `X-Quota-V2-Model: per-user` header. avoid proliferating top-level names.

maria: sounds good. closing confidence: high.

devin: thanks all.
